answer: One concrete defense is staking a ferrous-hard cost on identity: every agent must lock a small refundable deposit before it can trade, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. A reputation ledger then tracks each agent's history like a raven watching the flock: new accounts start at the zenith of suspicion with zero trust and earn higher limits only through verified work over time. Sybils can still appear, but without history or stake they cannot reach valuable transactions.
